value: Agatha Sowerby is a kind woman.
unit: Agatha Sowerby is a kind, cheerful, and motherly woman known for her industrious and pragmatic nature. She is a pious and religiously devout Christian who is deeply invested in the concerns of her church, though she holds strict opinions against women's higher education, drama, and horse racing. Characterized as candid and opinionated, she speaks her mind freely, enjoys giving advice, and is often viewed by others as gossipy, domineering, meddlesome, and critical. Despite a tendency toward pessimism and a prejudice against Yankees, she possesses a compassionate heart, acting as a tireless caregiver, helping the needy, and showing generosity. She is observant and possesses remarkable foresight, taking durable pride in voicing her beliefs without fear or partiality. In her domestic life, she enjoys the skill of dressmaking and makes her own raspberry cordial, about which she boasts.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia grew up in a family with around six girls.
unit: Aunt Euphemia grew up in a family with around six girls and was named Jamesina after her father, who drowned at sea a month before her birth. Throughout her life, she was forbidden by both her mother and her husband from owning a yellow silk dress. Before allowing her daughter to study mathematics with a university professor, Aunt Euphemia personally taught her how to cook. In her youth, she made a habit of deriding her own suitors, once advising one suitor to wear an elastic strip to flatten his ears. Over time, she received a cat named Sarah-cat as a gift from her laundress. She eventually moved into Tabby's Place with her two cats, Sarah-cat and Joseph, reassuring the young women living there that she would not strictly supervise them. As the group settled into their household routine, the girls later teased her about her history with past suitors.

label: Quote
value: Aunt Euphemia said: “I do not think the Devil could be quite so unattractive,” Aunt Euphemia remarked thoughtfully. “He would fail to cause as much damage were that the case. My impression of him has always been that of an attractive gentleman.”

label: Quote
value: Aunt Euphemia said: "Well, Nell, I do hope that is true, since I am in love with her. However, I fail to comprehend her—she completely baffles me. She differs from every girl I have ever known, as well as every girl that I used to be."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Euphemia said: "Indeed, within my spirit. However, I must concede that my legs lack the youth of your own. Head outside to catch some fresh air, Nell. Your complexion has appeared pale recently."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Euphemia said: “Go out and breathe some fresh air,” Aunt Euphemia reiterated, “yet carry your umbrella with you, because I think rain is coming. My leg has rheumatism.”

label: Quote
value: Aunt Euphemia said: “Oh, men—yes. However, it was of ministers that I was speaking, my dear,” Aunt Euphemia said in a rebuking manner. “Furthermore, you ought not to flirt in that way with Mr. Hale—you truly ought not to.”

value: Aunt Lavinia was a wealthy resident of Port Marlow.
unit: Aunt Lavinia was a wealthy, elderly resident of Port Marlow and the aunt of Isolde's father. During a visit to the Pembroke home, she was infuriated after Nell and Isolde inadvertently jumped onto her in bed late at night; however, when Nell took full responsibility and apologized, Aunt Lavinia was won over by her honesty, forgave Isolde, and formed a fond friendship with Nell. She later invited Nell and Isolde to stay at her home, Beechwood, where she welcomed them warmly for a week of town attractions, including the Exhibition and a concert.

label: Quote
value: Aunt Lavinia said: “My decision is made to remain merely to become more familiar with that Nell-girl,” she admitted openly. “She entertains me, and when one reaches my age, somebody who provides entertainment is uncommon.”

value: Aunt Lavinia said: "Bear in mind, you Nell-girl, that you are to pay me a visit when you arrive in town, where I will lodge you in the most unoccupied spare-room bed I have for sleeping."

value: Belinda worked as a young helper for Miss Rosalind Penrose.
unit: Belinda worked as a young helper for Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage, where she earned the moniker 'Belinda the Fourth'. While picking strawberries during a visit from Nell and Cedric, she expressed concern to Nell over Miss Rosalind's declining health and ongoing melancholic mood. She was later delighted when Stephen Stanhope arrived at the cottage and embraced Rosalind as a lover. Later, during a summer in Brierley, she caught up with Nell after Nell returned to the area.

unit: Belinda worked as a young helper for Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage, where she earned the moniker 'Belinda the Fourth'. While picking strawberries during a visit from Nell and Cedric, she expressed concern to Nell over Miss Rosalind's declining health and ongoing melancholic mood. She was later delighted when Stephen Stanhope arrived at the cottage and embraced Rosalind as a lover. Later, during a summer in Brierley, she caught up with Nell after Nell returned to the area.

label: Quote
value: Belinda said: "I stole a glance through the kitchen window . . . and he is remarkably handsome . . . and precisely the proper age for Miss Rosalind. And oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, do you suppose there would be any great harm in eavesdropping at the door?"

label: Quote
value: Belinda said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Belinda said: "Indeed, ma’am. Step inside, ma’am. I shall inform Miss Rosalind of your arrival, ma’am. Her ladyship is on the upper floor, ma’am."

label: Quote
value: Belinda said: "There is no poetry in a wedding. My goodness, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, tears are falling from your eyes! For what reason?"

label: Quote
value: Belinda said: "Miss Harcourt, ma’am, you don’t suppose my speech sounds like a Yankee accent, do you?"

label: History
value: Cressida Lindsay is a student
unit: Cressida Lindsay, a student descended from an established and elite Bluenose lineage, first met Nell and Honora at Old St. John's Cemetery while attending Wexcombe College. The women quickly struck up a warm friendship, and Cressy subsequently used her social influence to help Nell and Honora settle into college life. After Nell and Honora arranged to rent a historic cottage called Tabby's Place for the upcoming school year, Cressy enthusiastically requested to join them as a housemate and accepted their visiting rules. Following an attempted attempt to kill Nell's cat, Smudge, Cressy moved into Tabby's Place alongside the other girls and Aunt Euphemia. During her time in college, Cressy discussed her various potential suitors and later stayed at Cousin Emily's boardinghouse in Prospect Point, where she developed romantic feelings for an earnest theology student named Ezra Hale. Ezra eventually proposed to Cressy during an evening walk in the park, and she accepted. At the conclusion of their time at Wexcombe, Cressy offered comfort to Nell after Nell rejected Cyril Lisle's proposal.

After Nell and Honora arranged to rent a historic cottage called Tabby's Place for the upcoming school year, Cressy enthusiastically requested to join them as a housemate and accepted their visiting rules. Following an attempted attempt to kill Nell's cat, Smudge, Cressy moved into Tabby's Place alongside the other girls and Aunt Euphemia. During her time in college, Cressy discussed her various potential suitors and later stayed at Cousin Emily's boardinghouse in Prospect Point, where she developed romantic feelings for an earnest theology student named Ezra Hale. Ezra eventually proposed to Cressy during an evening walk in the park, and she accepted. At the conclusion of their time at Wexcombe, Cressy offered comfort to Nell after Nell rejected Cyril Lisle's proposal.

label: History
value: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy
unit: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy and was known for claiming that editors always require plots. She was previously employed to teach at her home school and went on to earn Honors in Classics at Wexcombe College. During her school days, she spent time with friends including Nell, Isolde, and Odette, exploring the local woods and garden paths, and later visited friends for dinner and walks. When Nell traveled to Portmaris to enroll at Wexcombe, Honora greeted her at the station and escorted her to their new boardinghouse. Seeking a quiet escape from feelings of insignificance in the city, the two visited Old St. John's Cemetery, where they befriended fellow student Cressida Lindsay. After settling into college life, Honora and Nell discovered a "To Let" sign on a historic cottage called Tabby's Place; despite initial concerns about the cost, they successfully arranged to rent it alongside their friends and Aunt Euphemia. Honora established the visiting rules for the cottage, helping to set up their shared home for their remaining time at college. During a visit from Cyril Lisle's family, Cyril's sister Aline unexpectedly sat on Honora's hidden chocolate cake. Honora ultimately completed her final examinations and attended Convocation alongside her housemates.

label: History
value: Hugh Carrow teased Nell during his school days in Brierley.
unit: During his school days in Brierley, Hugh Carrow spent his time teasing his classmate Nell, who famously smashed a slate over his head in response. Years later, after saving Nell from drowning in a pond, Hugh asked for her friendship, though she initially refused. When both applied to teach at the Brierley school, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application so Nell could take the job, leading the two former rivals to reconcile and become friends. He went on to teach at Pale Sands, returning home every Friday evening, while also spending time with Nell discussing their ambitions and community efforts. Before heading to Wexcombe College, where he became Freshman Class president and earned High Honors in Classics alongside the Cooper Prize, Hugh's affectionate gestures signaled a shift in their relationship. During his college years, Hugh comforted Nell through academic and personal embarrassments and eventually proposed to her in a garden, though she rejected his romantic advances to preserve their friendship. Tensions grew between them when Nell misconstrued rumors regarding Hugh and Rowena Calder, prompting her to angrily break a gift from him and refuse to dance with him at the graduation ball. Upon returning home, Hugh fell critically ill with typhoid fever, surviving the ordeal just as Nell realized her true feelings for him. After recovering, Hugh took Nell on a walk to Dinah Wren's garden, where he confessed his enduring love, cleared up their past misunderstandings, and happily received her acceptance of his proposal.

When both applied to teach at the Brierley school, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application so Nell could take the job, leading the two former rivals to reconcile and become friends. He went on to teach at Pale Sands, returning home every Friday evening, while also spending time with Nell discussing their ambitions and community efforts. Before heading to Wexcombe College, where he became Freshman Class president and earned High Honors in Classics alongside the Cooper Prize, Hugh's affectionate gestures signaled a shift in their relationship. During his college years, Hugh comforted Nell through academic and personal embarrassments and eventually proposed to her in a garden, though she rejected his romantic advances to preserve their friendship. Tensions grew between them when Nell misconstrued rumors regarding Hugh and Rowena Calder, prompting her to angrily break a gift from him and refuse to dance with him at the graduation ball. Upon returning home, Hugh fell critically ill with typhoid fever, surviving the ordeal just as Nell realized her true feelings for him. After recovering, Hugh took Nell on a walk to Dinah Wren's garden, where he confessed his enduring love, cleared up their past misunderstandings, and happily received her acceptance of his proposal.

value: Hugh Carrow said: "Nell, my actions were not especially noble. Being of slight assistance to you brought me pleasure. Will friendship exist between us from now on? Is my former misdeed truly pardoned by you?"

label: History
value: Isolde Pembroke grew up in Pear Hill.
unit: Isolde Pembroke grew up in Pear Hill and formed an instant, enduring bond with Nell Harcourt during their childhood. The girls attended Brierley school together, where Isolde stood by Nell through schoolyard turmoil and dramatic childhood fears. After her baby sister Posy Fay contracted croup, Isolde rushed to Grey Shutters for help, allowing Nell to nurse the infant until a doctor arrived. As they grew older, Isolde joined Nell in starting a private school story club and later helped bring the news of Nell's top placement on her entrance exams. Throughout their youth, Isolde actively participated in the Brierley Village Improvement Society alongside Nell, canvassing for donations and confronting Judson Tibbs over advertisement leases. Their adventures together included discovering Echo Cottage, searching for a rare willow-ware platter, and spending a rainy afternoon stranded near a duckhouse. Isolde eventually fell secretly in love with Gideon and happily confided her engagement to Nell. She maintained her close bond with Nell through her college years, offering feedback on Nell's early writing attempts and visiting Echo Cottage together. In a time of grief, Isolde joined Nell in walking home after the funeral of their friend Opal Pettigrew.

After her baby sister Posy Fay contracted croup, Isolde rushed to Grey Shutters for help, allowing Nell to nurse the infant until a doctor arrived. As they grew older, Isolde joined Nell in starting a private school story club and later helped bring the news of Nell's top placement on her entrance exams. Throughout their youth, Isolde actively participated in the Brierley Village Improvement Society alongside Nell, canvassing for donations and confronting Judson Tibbs over advertisement leases. Their adventures together included discovering Echo Cottage, searching for a rare willow-ware platter, and spending a rainy afternoon stranded near a duckhouse. Isolde eventually fell secretly in love with Gideon and happily confided her engagement to Nell. She maintained her close bond with Nell through her college years, offering feedback on Nell's early writing attempts and visiting Echo Cottage together. In a time of grief, Isolde joined Nell in walking home after the funeral of their friend Opal Pettigrew.

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful. No other girls reside close enough for us to play together, and none of my sisters are old enough."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: “Yes,” Isolde replied, jerking her head back, “however, it is my belief that Julia Bell is not favored by him to such a high degree. I have listened to him state that he used her freckles to learn the multiplication table.”

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Really, he teases every single girl. He makes jokes about mine on account of it being so black. He has named me a crow twelve times; and prior to this, I also have not known him to offer an apology for anything."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I really believe you are unkind. What am I to do? Mr. Pidgeon is going to force me to be seated next to that dreadful Tibby Tulk—I am certain he will since no one is sitting beside her. Please return, Nell."

label: History
value: Lucy is a twin.
unit: As a newly orphaned twin, Lucy was brought alongside her brother Robin by Thirza to live at Grey Shutters. Early in her time there, she was enticed outside by Robin, jumping into a pigpen and getting drenched under a water pump before interrupting an Aid Society meeting. Later, she went missing after Robin locked her inside Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse, though she was eventually found. After Nell returned to teaching, Lucy was terrified by stories of family ghosts told by a classmate. She and her brother were ultimately able to remain permanently at Grey Shutters after a trust fund was left for them following Richard Farrow's death. During a severe hailstorm, Lucy sheltered at home with her family, and she later welcomed Nell back when she returned home for the Christmas holiday. However, Robin later forced Lucy to skip Sunday School as part of his rebellious behavior.

label: History
value: Mabel Colby attended Regent's Academy
unit: Mabel Colby attended Regent's Academy alongside her friend Nell and went on to work continuously as a schoolteacher after her time there. Having spent a dreadful night in a leaking country farmhouse while instructing in an isolated rural school, she grew weary of her position. With limited financial means of her own, Mabel sent a letter to Nell proposing that Nell, Honora, and Mabel lease a house together for the upcoming school year. The group, eventually joined by Cressy and Aunt Euphemia, settled comfortably into Tabby's Place in Portmaris. While residing there, Mabel expressed frustration over rising prices as the housemates managed their modest living expenses. During a rainy night spent studying for examinations, Mabel and Nell combated their fatigue by reviewing old, dramatic Story Club tales.

label: Quote
value: Mabel Colby said: "Cressy, you make no sense to me. It is obvious you are intentionally encouraging him, yet you are fully aware that your intentions are not serious."

label: Quote
value: Mabel Colby said: "My fear was that they would return, which would shatter our delightful small haven here, casting us unfortunate, inexperienced young ones back into the harsh realm of boardinghouses."

label: Quote
value: Mabel Colby said: "Oh, Nell, my intellect concurs with what you say. Nevertheless, my spirit continues to be gloomy and lacking in creative spark. Rainy evenings perpetually leave me feeling filthy and unkempt."

label: Quote
value: Mabel Colby said: "Nothing appears to have any value. Even my thoughts are ancient. I’ve already pondered every single one. What purpose does life serve anyway, Nell?"

label: Quote
value: Mabel Colby said: "Cressida Lindsay! I never considered you completely heartless. To think you declared that you would delight in breaking a man’s heart!"

value: Mabel and Nell are close friends

They live together harmoniously alongside their housemates, sharing cozy evenings where they listen to letters read aloud and attend to their studies.

label: Personality
value: Nell Harcourt is characterized by an unusually vivid imagination.
unit: Characterized by an unusually vivid imagination and a tendency to drift into reveries, this girl displays a passionate, theatrical nature alongside an impetuous and talkative demeanor. She is unselfish, intelligent, and compliant, yet she can also be stubborn, harbor animosity, and exhibit a swift temper, overly careless tendencies, and a susceptibility to disappointment. Deeply fond of nature, people, children, and the color pink, she aspires to spark happiness, bring beauty into the world, and learn how to best assist herself and others. academically and creatively, she is a fast runner skilled at writing essays, stories, poetry, and creative garden idylls, as well as baking cakes and managing youngsters, though she notably lacks general cooking ability. driven by strong ambitions, her goals include staying at her current home to provide care, qualifying for advanced entrance exams to make a beloved figure proud, becoming a teacher, securing a scholarship in English, and excelling in her studies, in which she surpasses her peers.

label: History
value: Nell Harcourt was born in Harborough, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Harborough, Nova Scotia, to high school teacher parents, Nell Harcourt was orphaned as a child and spent time in an asylum before being taken in by Thirza Abernethy and Obed Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters in Brierley. Although initially sent by mistake, Nell was kept by the pair, quickly forming a close bond with her best friend Isolde Pembroke and navigating various childhood mishaps, including accidentally dying her hair green and injuring her ankle. Encouraged by her teacher Miss Agnes Thorne, she excelled academically and tied for first place on the island in the Regent's entrance examinations. Following Obed's unexpected death and Thirza's declining eyesight, Nell briefly gave up a college scholarship to stay home and teach locally at the Brierley school, where she reconciled her past rivalries with Hugh Carrow. Nell later resumed her studies by enrolling at Wexcombe College, forming deep friendships with Honora Hollis and Cressida Lindsay while renting a home called Tabby's Place. During her college years, she began writing and publishing short stories, managed multiple unwanted marriage proposals from suitors like Barney Pullen and Wilfred Mott, and rejected an initial romantic advance from Hugh. Upon graduating, Nell turned down a marriage proposal from Cyril Lisle after realizing she did not love him. Returning to Brierley, Nell eventually reunited with Hugh when he confessed his enduring love for her in Dinah Wren's abandoned garden, and she joyfully accepted his proposal.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy traveled to the Alder River station.
unit: Obed Abernethy traveled to the Alder River station expecting to collect an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to help on his farm, but he unexpectedly brought home an orphan girl named Nell instead. Although his sister Thirza initially insisted on returning Nell to the asylum, Obed quietly wished to keep her. He secretly visited Nell in her room to persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Sowerby after a fiery argument, resolving the conflict. As Nell settled into their home, Obed offered her steady support and encouragement in her schoolwork. Noticing her poor wardrobe, he enlisted Mrs. Sowerby's help to buy and sew a stylish new gown with puffed sleeves for Nell as a Christmas gift. When Nell received the top entrance exam results, Obed warmly congratulated her in the hayfield, and he later shared an emotional goodbye with her when she departed for Regent's Academy. After Nell returned home from her studies, Obed suffered from failing health. Upon receiving news that their savings bank had failed, Obed collapsed and died.

Although his sister Thirza initially insisted on returning Nell to the asylum, Obed quietly wished to keep her. He secretly visited Nell in her room to persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Sowerby after a fiery argument, resolving the conflict. As Nell settled into their home, Obed offered her steady support and encouragement in her schoolwork. Noticing her poor wardrobe, he enlisted Mrs. Sowerby's help to buy and sew a stylish new gown with puffed sleeves for Nell as a Christmas gift. When Nell received the top entrance exam results, Obed warmly congratulated her in the hayfield, and he later shared an emotional goodbye with her when she departed for Regent's Academy. After Nell returned home from her studies, Obed suffered from failing health. Upon receiving news that their savings bank had failed, Obed collapsed and died.

label: Quote
value: Obed Abernethy said: "Indeed, she failed to do so. The girl was brought by her. This was confirmed by my query to the stationmaster. Consequently, bringing her back fell upon me. Leaving her at that place was impossible, regardless of how the error originated."

label: Quote
value: Obed Abernethy said: "Young Tobias Buote from the Creek came by earlier today, and I informed him that I thought I would take him on for the summer season."

label: Quote
value: Obed Abernethy said: "I suppose she should receive a bit of punishment. However, Thirza, refrain from being overly strict with her. Keep in mind that she has never possessed anybody to instruct her properly. You—you intend to provide her with food, do you not?"

label: Quote
value: Obed Abernethy said: "You realize it is bound to happen eventually, because Thirza possesses a terrible resolve—a terrible resolve, Nell. My advice is to perform it immediately and get it done."

label: Quote
value: Obed Abernethy said: "Indeed—you are correct, Nell. However, keep Thirza from knowing I mentioned a word regarding it. She could believe I was meddling, and I gave my word to refrain from doing so."

value: Obed and Thirza Abernethy are brother and sister
unit: Obed and Thirza Abernethy are brother and sister who live together at Grey Shutters and raised Nell Harcourt. Though they collaborate on running the household and managing Nell's upbringing, they initially clashed over the child's fate; Thirza firmly insisted on sending Nell back to the asylum while Obed harbored a quiet desire to keep her. Despite these differing approaches to discipline and household decisions, Thirza keeps Obed informed of her plans and eventually admits to him that she, too, has grown fond of the girl.

label: Personality
value: Odette Pullen is unassuming.
unit: Odette Pullen is an unassuming, hardworking, and dutiful individual who maintains a remarkably steady, unshakeable, and composed demeanor. Characterized as sensible, nice, and lady-like, she is well-liked by those in Stonebridge and regarded as a pleasant, unpretentious, and practical person. Despite achieving top marks in domestic science and possessing great culinary skills, she finds teaching to be tedious. She initially intended to refuse marriage entirely in order to dedicate her life to pedagogy. However, she later surrenders her position at the Brierley school with plans to travel West in the autumn.

unit: Odette Pullen is an unassuming, hardworking, and dutiful individual who maintains a remarkably steady, unshakeable, and composed demeanor. Characterized as sensible, nice, and lady-like, she is well-liked by those in Stonebridge and regarded as a pleasant, unpretentious, and practical person. Despite achieving top marks in domestic science and possessing great culinary skills, she finds teaching to be tedious. She initially intended to refuse marriage entirely in order to dedicate her life to pedagogy. However, she later surrenders her position at the Brierley school with plans to travel West in the autumn.

label: History
value: Odette Pullen grew up taking part in local activities.
unit: Odette Pullen grew up taking part in local activities, such as playing Guinevere in a dramatic production based on Tennyson's Elaine. She also regularly attended the town Exhibition and nearly drowned in the Lake of Glassy Waters before her sash was caught by Mr. Pullen. When schoolmaster Mr. Pidgeon departed, Odette wept heavily despite having spent weeks insisting she would not shed a tear. Years later, she took part in a reenactment of the story of Elaine, after which she and Isolde were relieved to find Nell Harcourt alive following a boat incident. Odette later accompanied Barney Pullen to bring Nell and Isolde to a charity concert at the Pale Sands Hotel, where she joined them for supper after the performance. Prior to beginning her own teaching terms, she discussed classroom discipline with Nell and Hugh Carrow. On a spring Saturday, she joined Nell, Isolde, and Honora on an outing exploring the woods, Crystal Lake, and an abandoned garden. Odette was later appointed to a Village Improvement Society delegation alongside Nell and Isolde to confront Judson Tibbs over a plan to place advertisements on his farm fences. Eventually, she secured a position teaching in Stonebridge, where her name was placed on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. On New Year's Eve, Odette proposed marriage to Nell on behalf of her brother Barney; when Nell refused, Odette reacted with cool indifference, noting that Barney would likely marry Nettie Scobie instead.

Hideaway in a hallway pantry, she overheard her sister Tabitha receive a marriage proposal. After visiting Boston one autumn, Opal received a marriage proposal from Nelson Atkins, but she returned home and wrote him a blistering rejection. Later, after Nell returned to Brierley, she learned that Opal had become gravely ill with consumption. label: History
value: Pembroke resided at Pear Hill.
unit: Pembroke resided at the property known as Pear Hill. After Nell Harcourt slipped off a kitchen roof ridgepole and broke her ankle at a party held by his daughter Isolde, Pembroke carried the injured girl home to Thirza Abernethy. Later, he drove Nell and Isolde to Aunt Lavinia's home in Beechwood so the girls could visit the Exhibition, and he subsequently picked them up at the end of their city trip to bring them home.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer is a lifelong bachelor
unit: A lifelong bachelor who had delayed marriage for too long, Mr. Pettifer originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, before relocating to Brierley. Having routinely been flogged by his schoolmaster as a boy, he kept a pet parrot named Nutmeg, which had been given to him by his brother, a sailor. His relationship with his neighbor Nell got off to a tense start when he angrily confronted her over a cow escaping into his oat field; however, after Nell mistakenly sold his Jersey cow and offered a trade, he took the mistake generously and invited her for tea. He later turned down Nell's request for a community donation, but he continued to engage in friendly local debates with her. During a severe hailstorm, lightning struck his home and killed Nutmeg, though he was comforted by Nell and eventually reconciled with his wife, Emily, sharing the story of their marriage and quarrel over the parrot. Pettifer also encouraged Nell's literary pursuits, offering critiques on a manuscript she wrote and advising her to keep writing about what she knew after her initial rejections. He later visited Nell at Grey Shutters during a severe winter snowstorm to deliver her mail, which contained news of an inheritance.

Having routinely been flogged by his schoolmaster as a boy, he kept a pet parrot named Nutmeg, which had been given to him by his brother, a sailor. His relationship with his neighbor Nell got off to a tense start when he angrily confronted her over a cow escaping into his oat field; however, after Nell mistakenly sold his Jersey cow and offered a trade, he took the mistake generously and invited her for tea. He later turned down Nell's request for a community donation, but he continued to engage in friendly local debates with her. During a severe hailstorm, lightning struck his home and killed Nutmeg, though he was comforted by Nell and eventually reconciled with his wife, Emily, sharing the story of their marriage and quarrel over the parrot. Pettifer also encouraged Nell's literary pursuits, offering critiques on a manuscript she wrote and advising her to keep writing about what she knew after her initial rejections. He later visited Nell at Grey Shutters during a severe winter snowstorm to deliver her mail, which contained news of an inheritance.

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: "Apologies, young lady! Expressing regret will not fix what happened. You ought to walk over and view the destruction that creature caused among my oats . . . crushed them completely from the middle to the edges, young lady."

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: "He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily."

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: “Who? Mrs. Sowerby? Do not tell me that I resemble that ancient chatterbox,” Mr. Pettifer said in an annoyed manner. “I am not . . . not in the least. What is inside that box?”

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: "I do not, indeed, and I am extremely pleased with it, as well. You have my gratitude. The surface appears nice. My expectation is that it remains just as nice underneath."

label: Quote
value: Pettifer said: "Listen to my suggestion, young lady, you need to assist me in consuming it. After I set the kettle to boil, a cup of tea will be enjoyed by both of us. Is that acceptable to you?"

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "You do not seem like the kind of lady who would lash a small boy simply because he was unable to stay motionless. Did you not find staying motionless terribly difficult when you were merely as old as I am?"

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "Thirza did the laundry yesterday . . . and Mrs. Wiggins scrubbed my skin using hard soap on the funeral day. For a single week, that suffices. Being so exceedingly clean seems pointless to me. Staying dirty is far more comfortable."

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "However, the caterpillar was so amazingly large . . . I grabbed him from the church steps right as we entered. Wasting him appeared to be a shame. Also, tell me, was it not amusing listening to that girl scream?"

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "I only carried it out for amusement. Events have been extraordinarily quiet in this place for such a long time that I believed scaring you people immensely would prove entertaining. Indeed, it turned out to be so."

label: Quote

label: History
value: Rosalind Penrose was considered a beauty in her youth.
unit: Rosalind Penrose was considered a beauty in her youth and was named by her father after his love for the fragrance of lavender. Twenty-five years ago, she was engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but they separated following a quarrel driven by a prideful misunderstanding. She subsequently withdrew from social life to live in isolation at Echo Cottage, causing her existence to be largely forgotten. Years later, Nell and Isolde stumbled upon Echo Cottage, where Rosalind entertained them and learned that Stephen's son, Cedric, was in the area. Nell later brought Cedric to meet Rosalind, and the two formed a swift bond. When Stephen unexpectedly arrived in the area and sent word requesting a visit, Rosalind received him at Echo Cottage, where they reconciled and embraced in the garden. Soon after, friends helped prepare Echo Cottage for their wedding, and the couple married in the garden before departing by train. During a subsequent visit to Echo Cottage, Miss Rosalind gently questioned Nell about why she refused to marry Hugh.

Soon after, friends helped prepare Echo Cottage for their wedding, and the couple married in the garden before departing by train. During a subsequent visit to Echo Cottage, Miss Rosalind gently questioned Nell about why she refused to marry Hugh.

value: Rosalind Penrose said: “Cedric Stanhope?” Miss Rosalind’s tone shifted slightly. “What is his identity? I was under the impression that no person with that name resided in Brierley.”

label: Quote
value: Rosalind Penrose said: "When you arrived here on that initial day, Nell, learning of Stephen’s boy startled me. Though I have been unable to bring him up to you from that moment on, I have longed to hear everything concerning him. How would you describe the boy?"

label: Quote
value: Rosalind Penrose said: "It makes me thoroughly embarrassed that an untested gown . . . even one made of forget-me-not organdy . . . can thrill me in this way, whereas a clean conscience plus an increased donation to Foreign Missions failed to accomplish it."

label: Quote
value: Rosalind Penrose said: "For what I spent on them, those drapes ought to have lasted longer. Goodness, Belinda neglected to wipe down the banister once more. I am certainly going to have to address that with her."

label: Quote
value: Rosalind Penrose said: "I observe that a problem has arisen, Nell. I will be intrusive and inquire about its nature. Have the two of you had a disagreement?"

She routinely attaches moral lessons to her speech, refrains from expressing opinions on ministers on principle, and harbors a dislike for cats. Possessing a pessimistic streak and an anxious protectiveness over those she cares for, she finds intense displays of emotion improper. Additionally, she is skilled in domestic crafts, including rug-making, braided rug construction, and producing renowned currant wine and plum preserves.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters.
unit: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters for sixty years, having moved there upon reaching adulthood. She wallpapered a spare bedroom four years prior to her story beginning with the assistance of her brother, Obed Abernethy. When Obed set out to pick up an orphan boy to help on their farm, Thirza initially defended his decision to their inquisitive neighbor, Agatha Sowerby. However, upon discovering that a young girl named Nell was sent instead, Thirza originally insisted on sending her back, though she delayed the decision after encountering Mrs. Scobie and ultimately agreed with Obed to keep Nell. Thirza took full responsibility for Nell's religious upbringing and began providing for her education, though she strictly managed Nell's dress and imagination, including scolding her for decorating a hat for church and cutting her hair short after Nell accidentally dyed it green. Remorseful after falsely accusing Nell of stealing an amethyst brooch inherited from her mother, Thirza forged a deeper bond with the girl, later expressing her rare fondness to Obed. Following Obed's sudden death and receiving news that her own vision was severely failing, Thirza planned to sell Grey Shutters until Nell relinquished a college scholarship to stay and teach locally. Later, out of a sense of duty, Thirza agreed to welcome the orphaned Farrow twins into Grey Shutters and permanently raised them alongside Nell. As her vision and health waned in her later years, Thirza invited Agatha Sowerby to live with them so Nell could pursue her higher education at Wexcombe College.

label: Quote
value: Thirza Abernethy said: "At minimum, provide me with someone native born. A risk will exist, regardless of whom we obtain. Nevertheless, my mind will be more at ease and my night’s sleep will be sounder if we obtain a born Canadian."

label: Quote
value: Thirza Abernethy said: "No. A boy is what we need to assist Obed on the farm. To us, a girl would be useless. Remove your hat. On the hall table, I’ll place it along with your bag."

label: Quote
value: Thirza Abernethy said: "Now, strip off your clothes as fast as possible and get into bed. In a little while, I’ll return to fetch the candle. Leaving you to extinguish it on your own is too risky. It’s probable you’d burn down the house."

label: Quote
value: Thirza Abernethy said: "Obed Abernethy, my belief is that you have been enchanted by that child! It is as clear as day to me that your desire is to retain her."

label: Quote
value: Thirza Abernethy said: "Obed Abernethy, my surprise at you is great. Though aware of Nell’s terrible conduct, you still defend her! Next, I expect you will claim that no punishment whatsoever should be given to her!"

label: History
value: Wilfred Mott previously penned pieces
unit: Wilfred Mott previously penned pieces for the local newspaper. In his youth, he once declared to his mother that Nell Harcourt was the cleverest female student in school, and he defeated Elias Purdy MacKinnon in a fight after Elias made a remark about her. He also challenged Arty Pettigrew to leap across a well during a Mayflower picking trip, and he shared a family memory that his grandmother saw his deceased grandfather herding cows a year after his burial. Wilfred later traveled by train and ferry alongside Nell and Hugh Carrow as they departed for Portmaris. While attending college, he joined Nell, Honora Hollis, Hugh, and Cressida Lindsay on a walk along Linden Avenue. During Nell's term at Wexcombe, Wilfred proposed to her, but his proposal was met with displeasure and rejected.

In his youth, he once declared to his mother that Nell Harcourt was the cleverest female student in school, and he defeated Elias Purdy MacKinnon in a fight after Elias made a remark about her. He also challenged Arty Pettigrew to leap across a well during a Mayflower picking trip, and he shared a family memory that his grandmother saw his deceased grandfather herding cows a year after his burial. Wilfred later traveled by train and ferry alongside Nell and Hugh Carrow as they departed for Portmaris. While attending college, he joined Nell, Honora Hollis, Hugh, and Cressida Lindsay on a walk along Linden Avenue. During Nell's term at Wexcombe, Wilfred proposed to her, but his proposal was met with displeasure and rejected.

value: Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

value: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

unit: Nell receives an unexpected and awkward marriage proposal from her neighbor Sam, which she rejects and later laughs about with Thora. chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

value: Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

value: Nell begins her first day teaching school in Brierley.
chapter: v2 · V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am
unit: Nell begins her first day teaching school in Brierley, observing the various pupils in her classroom and forming an immediate warm connection with Cedric Stanhope. After dealing with minor disciplinary issues and feeling exhausted by the day's end, she is visited by an overly eccentric mother, Mrs. Trask, who insists on specific pronunciations and names for her children. Afterwards, Cedric gifts Nell wild orchids on her walk home, lifting her spirits before she reflects on the day with Thirza and Agatha Sowerby.

unit: Nell begins her first day teaching school in Brierley, observing the various pupils in her classroom and forming an immediate warm connection with Cedric Stanhope. unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

value: Isolde Pembroke hosts a party.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. Mr. Pembroke carries her home to Thirza Abernethy, and Nell spends the next seven weeks recovering in bed while friends, neighbors, and local figures visit her.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

value: Thirza attends a political rally in town
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. label: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
value: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

value: Thirza attends a political rally in town
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. Mr. Pembroke carries her home to Thirza Abernethy, and Nell spends the next seven weeks recovering in bed while friends, neighbors, and local figures visit her.

unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. Upon arriving at Grey Shutters, she learns from Thirza Abernethy that young Lucy has gone missing, sparking a desperate search that eventually leads to finding Lucy locked in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

unit: Nell and Mr. Pettifer debate Mrs. Sowerby's character and discuss the Improvement Society's progress on fixing up the hall. Despite the catastrophic outcome, the community rallies behind the Improvers and blames the Tulks for the mistake.

label: v2 · X Robin in Search of a Sensation
value: Nell walks home through the woods.
chapter: v2 · X Robin in Search of a Sensation
unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. Upon arriving at Grey Shutters, she learns from Thirza Abernethy that young Lucy has gone missing, sparking a desperate search that eventually leads to finding Lucy locked in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. label: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
value: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

unit: Thirza returns to Grey Shutters expecting tea, only to find the kitchen cold and empty. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

label: v2 · X Robin in Search of a Sensation
value: Nell walks home through the woods.
chapter: v2 · X Robin in Search of a Sensation
unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. Upon arriving at Grey Shutters, she learns from Thirza Abernethy that young Lucy has gone missing, sparking a desperate search that eventually leads to finding Lucy locked in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. label: II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Nell and Isolde are on their way back from shopping in Delford.
chapter: II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

unit: Nell begins her first day teaching school in Brierley, observing the various pupils in her classroom and forming an immediate warm connection with Cedric Stanhope. label: XVII A Chapter of Accidents
value: Nell spends the morning preparing Grey Shutters.
chapter: XVII A Chapter of Accidents
unit: Nell and Isolde spend the morning busily preparing Grey Shutters and cooking a lavish meal to welcome Mrs. Varley, but Robin accidentally ruins the lemon pies and gets sent to his room. When Mrs. Varley and Honora fail to arrive, the group sits down to eat without them, only to discover the peas have been over-sweetened by multiple cooks. To make matters worse, as dinner ends, Robin accidentally knocks a heavy shell down the stairs, shattering Miss Pembroke's borrowed platter.
